series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/2] mm: refactor find_next_best_node to find_next_best_node_in
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the find_next_best_node() function to find_next_best_node_in(), which takes an explicit candidates nodemask instead of relying on N_MEMORY. This change enables building fallback lists with non-N_MEMORY candidates, but does not introduce any functional changes as callers still select from N_MEMORY. The refactor affects three files: mm/internal.h, mm/memory-tiers.c, and mm/page_alloc.c.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/2] mm/page_alloc: refactor build_node_zonelist() out of build_zonelists()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the build_zonelists() function in the Linux kernel's page allocation module to extract a new function, build_node_zonelist(), which constructs per-node fallback lists from candidate nodemasks. This change allows for building new zonelists based on node masks instead of just using the default N_MEMORY node state list. The patch does not introduce any functional changes and maintains the same behavior as before.

review_comments.author: Vlastimil (SUSE)
review_comments.summary: Reviewer suggested moving pr_cont() printing into build_node_zonelist() and eliminating the node_order array, which would require modifying build_zonelists_in_node_order() to process nodes piece-meal
review_comments.raw_body:
LGTM, but, while we're at it, could we just do the pr_cont() printing in
build_node_zonelist() itself (maybe behind a flag if you don't want to print
from future new caller) so it doesn't need to pass nr_nodes back to
build_zonelists(). Then also the node_order array could live in
build_node_zonelist() itself?

Actually I wonder if we could get ride of the node_order array completely.
It would mean the loop processing in build_zonelists_in_node_order() would
have to be done piece-meal in build_node_zonelist() itself. But seems
feasible? Depends on how you intend to reuse/extend the new functions later,
I guess...

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged that the patch needs further testing and experimentation to see how well it generalizes, indicating a need for revision.
review_comments.raw_body:
I can take a look.  We've been testing a couple different things, will
see how well things generalize (private node fallback lists, inverted
fallback lists for proactive reclaim node ordering, some other stuff).

~Gregory

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch refactors the zonelist constructors and iterators in the Linux kernel to make them more flexible and modular. The changes include extracting a new function `find_next_best_node_in` that takes an explicit candidate set, and moving the per-node construction loop out of `build_zonelists` into a separate function `build_node_zonelist`. These changes allow for building zonelists over custom sets of nodes and iterating over them in fallback order. The refactoring is intended to be functional equivalent to the original code, but with improved modularity and flexibility.
